text.p: Houston Exploration Co Thursday said it was awarded 13 leases from the federal oil and gas lease sale number 161, held September 25, 1996.

Houston Exploration's leases, which run for five to eight years, include 60,480 acres gross, (51,168 acres net) in the shallow waters (up to 600 feet) of the Gulf of Mexico and 7,685 acres gross (7,685 acres net) in the deeper waters of the outer continental shelf. Houston Exploration's offshore properties now total 295,854 acres gross (210,138 acres net).
Houston Exploration will serve as operator on 12 of the 13 blocks and has a 100 percent working interest in nine of the leases.

"We are extremely pleased with the results of this lease sale," said James Floyd, president and chief executive officer of Houston Exploration. "Many of these leases are concentrated in the Marg. A' trend of the Gulf, a geological trend that has had a number of significant discoveries."

"Our evaluation on these blocks prior to the lease sale was very encouraging and we are in the process of selecting drill sites. Given their proximity to each other and existing programs, we expect we will be able to economically explore in this high-impact region," he said.
Drilling in these areas is expected to begin in late 1997.
The leases were purchased at a capital cost of about $6 million.
